title: Rybakina beats Gauff, clinches No. 1 ranking ahead of US Open final vs. Sabalenka on September 13
dek: Elena Rybakina defeated Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the US Open semifinal on September 11, guaranteeing the world No. 1 ranking. She will face top seed Aryna Sabalenka in Saturday's final, a matchup between the top two seeds, the first such final at the US Open since 2013.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Rybakina's semifinal victory over Gauff secures her ascent to world No. 1 when rankings update on Monday, September 14, and sets up a final against Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2.
bottom_line: Rybakina and Sabalenka contest the September 13 final with contrasting trajectories: Rybakina ascending to the rankings summit after breakthrough form at the US Open; Sabalenka defending consecutive championships on her best surface but facing a competitor who has now beaten her in a major final this year. The outcome will confirm whether Rybakina's momentum carries through a major final, or whether Sabalenka's hard-court mastery prevails.
body: Elena Rybakina advanced to the US Open final by defeating Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the semifinal on September 11, per BBC Sport. The victory guarantees Rybakina's rise to world No. 1 when the rankings update on Monday, September 14, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top.

Rybakina will face Sabalenka in Saturday's final, a championship match between the top two seeds. According to BBC Sport, this marks the first time the top two women's seeds have contested a US Open final since Serena Williams defeated Victoria Azarenka in 2013.

Sabalenka claimed the other semifinal berth by defeating Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2, per BBC Sport. Sabalenka dropped just one set en route to the final and has not been defeated in New York since falling in the 2023 final to Gauff. She pounded 29 winners to Pegula's 12 in the second set of their semifinal.

Rybakina enters the final seeking her third Grand Slam title, according to BBC Sport. She won Wimbledon in 2022 and defeated Sabalenka in January's Australian Open final. However, Sabalenka holds the overall head-to-head advantage with 10 wins in 17 meetings, per BBC Sport. Most recently in 2026, Sabalenka beat Rybakina in the Indian Wells final and in the Miami semifinals, though Rybakina mounted a comeback in Melbourne after Sabalenka led 3-0 in the deciding set.

Sabalenka arrives as a four-time major singles winner seeking a third consecutive US Open title, a feat accomplished by only three women in the Open era, per BBC Sport. She won the Sunshine Double at Indian Wells and Miami in March but struggled at other majors, suffering a quarterfinal defeat at Roland Garros and a fourth-round exit at Wimbledon. Sabalenka also broke the Open era record for the most consecutive Grand Slam hard-court finals, reaching every major final on her favored surface since the 2023 Australian Open.

Rybakina said after the semifinal, according to BBC Sport: "I took a deep breath and just told myself I needed to fight and show good tennis." She added: "I definitely need to step my game up in the final, serve better than today, stay aggressive and really go for my shots." Sabalenka told BBC Sport after defeating Pegula: "I was super desperate." She continued: "It feels for me, talking about Grand Slams, like a last push of the season. I wanted it badly to go to the finals, and of course, I want to go all the way."
